change.title: ao-replay/8720
change.description: perf(spawn): stop new chats waiting on repeat git downloads
change.author: ronish

findings.title: Repos with no usable cached HEAD pay a full lookup on every start, and the 5s bound is per repo
findings.body:
`resolveAutomaticDefault` only short-circuits when `Inspect` succeeds (workspace.go:2055). A repo with no cached HEAD (a never-fetched clone, or an offline first run) falls through to `Resolve` on every start, even inside `automaticDefaultRecheck`. The comment at 2063-2064 says an offline machine does not start another lookup for every start in the window. That holds only when a cached HEAD exists.

The 5s budget is created per `ResolveDefaultBranch` call (workspace.go:198). The caller loops over all targets before its shared `fetchCtx` starts (manager.go:2236-2251). The worst case for a workspace project with N unreachable, uncached child repos is therefore about N×5s of resolution, then up to 5s of fetches, on every spawn.

That is still better than the old unbounded `Resolve(ctx, ctx, ...)`. The comments at manager.go:2234-2235 ("which the adapter bounds") and workspace.go:2063 overstate the bound. Either tighten the comments, or share one deadline across the targets in the resolve loop. A negative cache for failed lookups is another option.

findings.title: No test for the unreachable-remote path or the Fetched=false fallback
findings.body:
The new window logic has an explicit offline branch: the attempt is recorded even when `Resolve` errors (workspace.go:2063-2068). `Resolve` also falls back to the cached HEAD with `SourceCachedRemoteHead` when the fetch fails, and that case must report `Fetched=false`. The tests here cover only the all-success path. Add a case where `ls-remote` or `fetch` fails and check three things: the cache answer is returned, `Fetched` is false, and a second resolve inside the window issues no new lookup.

`TestWorktreeRefsReuseTheRefreshLookup` (line 136) has a related weakness. The fake returns success for every unmatched `rev-parse`, so `FindCachedRemoteBranch` sees `ao/work` as existing. The test never asserts `seedRef`, so that is not checked.

findings.title: Overlapping background fetches of the same base are possible
findings.body: `defaultBranchFetchedRecently` stamps `defaultBranchFetchedAt` when the fetch is attempted. The background fetch is allowed up to `defaultBranchBackgroundFetchTimeout` (1 min, manager.go:2324), but the skip window is only 30s. A slow fetch that is still running at +30s lets the next start launch a second `git fetch` of the same refspec (`defaultBranchFresh` is still true because freshness is only recorded on success). Two concurrent fetches into the same remote-tracking ref can hit ref-lock contention. The loser is only logged as a warning, so it self-heals. An in-flight marker per key, or recording the attempt time as the dedupe key until the fetch completes, would avoid it.

contracts.action: Automatic default branch resolved from cached HEAD with a background `ls-remote` lookup (new `resolveAutomaticDefault`, `RefreshRemoteHead`)
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously `ResolveDefaultBranch` and `resolveWorktreeRefs` each called `gitdefault.Resolver.Resolve` (live `ls-remote`, fetch of the branch, set cached HEAD) on every call. `Resolve` at resolver.go:139-194 is still the path taken when the cache is unusable.
contracts.before_after: Before: two live lookups plus fetches per spawn (refresh, then worktree creation). After: within `automaticDefaultRecheck` (10 min) both answer from `Inspect`. Past it, the refresh path answers from the cache and starts one background `RefreshRemoteHead`. The attempt is recorded before the goroutine starts, so concurrent spawns launch one lookup. Worktree creation (`background=false`) past the window with a usable cache waits for the live lookup as before.
contracts.visible_effect: Spawn no longer waits for `ls-remote` and fetch when a cached HEAD exists. A remote that renames its default branch is picked up only by the start after the background lookup, and only after the 10-min window. Until then the session is seeded from the old default.
contracts.failure_mode: Background lookup failure is only logged via `logf` (workspace.go:2083). The window stays marked current for the full 10 min, so the cached default is kept. If the cached HEAD is unusable, `Inspect` fails and `Resolve` runs with the 5s budget on every start (see the finding at workspace.go:2062). The goroutine uses `context.Background()` with a 5s timeout, so it cannot hang past 5s and is not cancelled on daemon shutdown.

contracts.action: Manager skips or backgrounds the base-ref fetch using `Fetched` and a 10-min fresh window
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing 30s `defaultBranchFetchedRecently` skip at manager.go:2269 and the synchronous `FetchDefaultBranch` at manager.go:2278. Resolution is still called first for every target at manager.go:2237, so each repo's own ref is resolved before any fetch.
contracts.before_after: Before: every spawn outside the 30s window fetched synchronously within `fetchCtx` (5s shared). After: `Fetched=true` records the fetch and skips it. A base last fetched successfully under 10 min ago is used as is, and the fetch runs via `runInBackground` with `backgroundContext` and a 1-min timeout. Otherwise (first start, after a restart, or past 10 min) the fetch is synchronous as before, and success records freshness.
contracts.visible_effect: A start inside the fresh window is not delayed by a fetch. The session branch is seeded from a base that can be up to 10 min old, with no indication to the user. Creation reads the ref while the background fetch may still be updating it.
contracts.failure_mode: A background fetch failure is logged as a warning and does not update freshness. After 10 min without a success, the next start waits for the fetch again. The map state is in-memory, so a daemon restart resets it. `runInBackground` counts the worker in `backgroundWorkers`, and the context derives from `backgroundContext`, so shutdown cancels it. Overlapping background fetches are possible (see the finding at manager.go:2274).

contracts.action: What bounds the whole wait: automatic-default resolution in the spawn refresh path
contracts.equivalent_path: The refresh's shared `fetchCtx` at manager.go:2255, which bounds all fetches to one 5s deadline.
contracts.before_after: Before: `Resolve(ctx, ctx, repo)` had no time budget beyond the caller's context. After: each `ResolveDefaultBranch` call creates its own 5s `remoteCtx`, shared between `ls-remote` and fetch inside `Resolve`. The manager calls it once per target in a sequential loop before `fetchCtx` starts, so the bound is per repo, not per spawn.
contracts.visible_effect: Worst case for a workspace project with N repos that need a live lookup: about N×5s before the fetch phase, then up to 5s of fetches. A single-repo project is bounded at 5s plus 5s. Cached repos answer without waiting.
contracts.failure_mode: The wait is not silent in logs: failures are logged and the spawn continues with the adapter fallback. Nothing shows the user the delay. Repos with no cached HEAD re-pay the wait on every start.

summary: The change is coherent and its core flows check out against the code: `Fetched` skips a duplicate fetch, the Inspect-based window skips repeat lookups, and the background fetch and lookup are tracked and cancellable. I found no blocker or silent data-loss bug. Two things are worth a look. First, the 5s bound on automatic-default resolution is per repo, so a workspace project with many cold or unreachable repos can wait N×5s per spawn. Repos with no cached HEAD re-pay it on every start, which contradicts the comment at workspace.go:2063. Second, background fetches of the same base can overlap, because the 30s skip window is shorter than the 1-min fetch timeout. The tests miss the offline and fallback paths, and one fake treats every unmatched `rev-parse` as existing. The deliberate tradeoff of seeding sessions from a base up to 10 min old is listed under judgement.
